title: Discovering Our Past: A History of the United States
edition: 2018 (Networks; school ISBN is the full-survey student edition)

sources.what: district pacing guide (St. Johns County, FL, 2018-19) keyed to chapters of the 2018 Early Years, Florida Edition
teacher class page naming Discovering Our Past (2013) with chapter numbers 10, 12, 13 (teacher's own chapter labels)
Bookshare record confirming ISBN 9780076680504 = Discovering Our Past: History of the United States, grades 6-8, 2018
publisher program page (full survey, grades 6-8, author team, components)

summary: A middle-school U.S. history survey in McGraw Hill's Networks program, built around essential questions, with chapters divided into short lessons. The full-survey edition runs from the first Americans to the present; the Early Years and Modern Times splits break at Reconstruction (1877).

toc.label: Chapter 2
toc.title: Exploring the Americas
toc.covers: European exploration and the Spanish, French, and English presence in the Americas.

toc.label: Chapters 3-4
toc.title: Colonial Era
toc.covers: Founding of the English colonies and colonial life, government, and conflict up to the French and Indian War.

toc.label: Chapter 5
toc.title: Toward Revolution
toc.covers: British taxes, colonial resistance, and the road to independence.

toc.label: Chapter 6
toc.title: The American Revolution
toc.covers: The War of Independence from the early campaigns to the Treaty of Paris.

toc.label: Chapters 7-8
toc.title: New Republic and Constitution
toc.covers: The Articles of Confederation, the Constitutional Convention, and the Constitution and Bill of Rights.

toc.label: Chapter 9
toc.title: The Federalist Era
toc.covers: Washington's and Adams's presidencies, Hamilton's program, and the first political parties.

toc.label: Chapter 10
toc.title: The Jefferson Era
toc.covers: Jefferson's presidency, the Louisiana Purchase and Lewis and Clark, and the War of 1812.

toc.label: Chapter 12
toc.title: The Jackson Era
toc.covers: Jacksonian democracy, Indian Removal, and conflicts over the national bank and states' rights.

toc.label: Chapter 13
toc.title: Manifest Destiny
toc.covers: Westward expansion to Oregon, Texas, and California and the Mexican-American War (paced with lesson 11.2).

toc.label: Chapters 14-15
toc.title: North and South & Reform
toc.covers: The industrial North and immigration, the cotton South and slavery, and reform movements such as abolition and women's rights (paced with lesson 11.1).

toc.label: Chapter 16
toc.title: Toward Civil War
toc.covers: Sectional crises of the 1850s, the Dred Scott decision, Lincoln's election, and secession.

toc.label: Chapter 17
toc.title: The Civil War
toc.covers: The course of the Civil War from Fort Sumter to Appomattox, including emancipation.

toc.label: Chapter 18
toc.title: Reconstruction
toc.covers: Rebuilding the South, the Reconstruction amendments, and the end of Reconstruction.

notes: No publisher TOC for the U.S. book was found (only the World History companion's). The headings above are a Florida district's topic labels keyed to chapter numbers of the 2018 Early Years, Florida Edition. They are not confirmed chapter titles. The numbering looks stable across editions: a teacher page using the 2013 national edition also has the Jefferson era at Chapter 10, the Jackson era at 12, and Manifest Destiny at 13. A Florida edition could still add or split chapters, though. Chapter 1 (the First Americans), Chapter 11, and every chapter after Reconstruction (about 1877 to the present) are missing. A teacher should check this against the school's copy before relying on it.
